title: FaceIQ Labs — Harmony & facial ratios
notes: 71 public guides; 33 front + 33 side scored, five supporting; formulas/definitions public; per-analysis reference ranges, scoring curves and weights are not publicly enumerated.

title: FaceIQ Labs — Understanding your scores
notes: 0–10 scale, 5≈average; Harmony ranges said to be adjusted for gender/ethnicity; power-mean aggregation; exact parameters undisclosed.

title: FaceIQ Labs — How FaceIQ Labs works
notes: Front+profile workflow; roughly 60/40 front/side contribution; gender/ethnicity select reference settings.

title: FaceIQ Labs — Why is my rating inaccurate?
notes: Landmark placement is stated as major error source; ideal ranges/weights described as research-informed but model-based.

title: FaceIQ Labs — Taking the right photos
notes: Recommends ~2 m, rear camera, 2× zoom, eye level, neutral expression, even light, true frontal/profile.

title: FaceIQ Labs — Angularity
notes: Five 0–10 vision-morph assessments; 10 described as ideal; same rating criteria by gender though morphs differ.

title: FaceIQ Labs — Dimorphism
notes: 0–10 opposite-sex-typical→same-sex-typical morph; public page lists 11 traits although scores page says 10.

title: FaceIQ Labs — Features
notes: Vision assessments rated 0–10 where 10 means issue absent; category caps disclosed, exact model validation not public.

title: Looksmax.org — How To Calculate Frontal Facial Harmony
notes: Explicit T1–T6/7 tables. User-generated, internally inconsistent in places. Never treat as scientific or FaceIQ.

title: Facial Analysis Formula PDF (Looksmax attachment)
notes: Explicit frontal/profile tiers and weights. Contains ambiguous units/inequalities and differs from related forum post in some cells.

title: Farkas et al. International anthropometric study of facial morphology in various ethnic groups/races
notes: 1470 healthy adults aged 18–30, 25 ethnic/racial groups, direct anthropometry; normative morphology, not attractiveness.

title: Farkas et al. Vertical and horizontal proportions of the face: revision of neoclassical canons
notes: 153 young North American Caucasian adults; most neoclassical canons did not describe average faces.

title: Le et al. Proportionality in Asian and North American Caucasian faces
notes: Direct comparison of Chinese, Vietnamese, Thai and North American Caucasian adults; classic canons infrequent and population-dependent.

title: Fang et al. A systematic review of interethnic variability in facial dimensions
notes: 2359 individuals across 27 ethnic groups; greatest variability included forehead height, interocular distance, nasal width.

title: Khoshab et al. Historical Tools of Anthropometric Facial Assessment
notes: Systematic raw-data analysis; no ethnic/gender group consistently approximated neoclassical canons and Phi.

title: Pallett, Link & Lee — New “golden” ratios for facial beauty
notes: Controlled image-manipulation experiments: ~36% vertical eye-mouth/face length and ~46% interocular/face width optimized ratings for that paradigm.

title: Wen et al. Inter-Ethnic/Racial Facial Variations: systematic review & Bayesian meta-analysis
notes: 38 photogrammetric studies; sex- and broad population-specific norms; significant differences for several profile angles.

title: Reliability and Accuracy of 2D Photogrammetry: A Comparison With Direct Measurement
notes: 96 adults; 2D reliable for many dimensions but bizygomatic and bigonial breadth showed clinically significant disagreement.

title: Ward et al. Nasal Distortion in Short-Distance Photographs: The Selfie Effect
notes: Model predicts ~30% larger nose/bizygomatic ratio at 12 in vs orthographic; ~5 ft essentially removes modeled distortion.

title: Geniole et al. Meta-analyses of facial width-to-height ratio
notes: Standard fWHR = face width / upper-face height; tiny sex difference (d=.11, n=10,853), BMI association. Definition is not identical to FaceIQ adaptation.

title: Armijo et al. Defining the ideal nasolabial angle
notes: Small manipulated-photo preference study: male 95.96±2.57°, female 97.7±2.32°.

title: Brown & Guyuron — Redefining the ideal nasolabial angle: expert analysis
notes: Rhinoplasty Society ratings: 95% CI ideal means 93.9–97.3° male; 96.8–100.2° female.

title: Sinno et al. The ideal nasolabial angle in rhinoplasty
notes: 98 general-population volunteers; most aesthetic ~97.0±6.3° male and 104.9±4.0° female; preferences varied with demographics.

title: Preferred Nasolabial Angle in Rhinoplasty: cross-sectional analysis
notes: 197 Canada/Saudi/Kuwaiti/Lebanese respondents; mean preferred 97.1±6.39° male, 109.5±5.32° female.

title: Naini et al. Nasofrontal Angle and Nasal Dorsal Aesthetics
notes: Idealized male Caucasian silhouette; ~130° ideal, 127–142° acceptable. Not a population norm.

title: Naini et al. Nasofacial angle and nasal prominence
notes: Idealized male Caucasian silhouette; ~30° ideal, 27–36° acceptable.

title: Naini et al. Mentolabial angle and aesthetics
notes: Idealized male Caucasian silhouette; ~107–118° most attractive; up to ~140° acceptable.

title: Naini et al. Submental-Cervical Angle
notes: Idealized profile silhouette; 90–100° most attractive, 90–105° acceptable.

title: Taylor et al. Quantitative facial asymmetry using 3D photogrammetry
notes: 100 healthy subjects; mirrored-surface RMSD 0.80±0.24 mm; high interobserver reliability for quantitative measure.

title: Expanding the Classic Facial Canons: Quantifying Intercanthal Distance
notes: Systematic review, 67 studies, 22,638 participants; pooled ICD differs substantially by population and often sex/measurement method.

title: Assessment of the golden proportion in natural facial esthetics: systematic review
notes: No significant association between golden ratio and facial evaluation scores across ethnicities; facial height proportions did not consistently follow Phi.

title: Legan & Burstone — Soft tissue cephalometric analysis for orthognathic surgery
notes: Established clinical soft-tissue cephalometric framework; angular conventions may be supplementary/incompatible with photographic systems.

title: Reliability of analytical reference lines for esthetically pleasing lip position
notes: S-, E-, and Burstone lines were most consistent in studied Chinese samples; population-specific interpretation required.

title: Age-related changes in lip position relative to the esthetic plane
notes: Large cross-sectional sample (n=2961) demonstrates age is relevant for E-line lip position.
